verdict.root_cause: A platform-automation traffic-shaping container was attached to cart's network namespace at 01:03:28, applying a fixed 300ms egress delay with zero jitter on eth0, and was still attached at onset (01:07:46) with no matching removal [tr_af88a5d99977]. Every cart response therefore pays a constant ~300ms network penalty that is invisible inside cart itself: cart's own handler self-time, Redis and flagd egress are all single-digit milliseconds [tr_ddbe17b074c8], its logs show only normal info-level cart-store operations with no errors or connection failures [tr_52ccaf6495ea], and its error ratio is flat at zero, actually below baseline [tr_c28534010e66, tr_f36a7089e42c]. The failure is experienced by cart's callers — frontend, frontend-proxy, checkout and load-generator all alerted at or just after onset — because they wait on a cart call that is slow in the wire path rather than in the service. Frontend has no change of its own to explain it [tr_fab33a03583f]. This is cart-side injected network latency propagating up the checkout path.
verdict.reasoning: The symptom set is a latency incident with no errors anywhere at the suspected service: cart returns zero error spans through the whole window and emits only normal info-level store operations, so cart is neither crashing, refusing, nor losing its Valkey backend [tr_c28534010e66, tr_52ccaf6495ea, tr_f36a7089e42c]. Cart is also not silent, which separates this from a process freeze, and its logs contain no 'cannot reach' complaints, which separates it from a partition on cart's own outbound dependencies. The only recorded act in the window is a repeating attach/remove of a traffic-shaping container that sets a constant 300ms eth0 delay, with the final attach four minutes before onset and no removal after it [tr_af88a5d99977]. That mechanism explains the exact shape of the evidence: a delay applied in the network namespace lands outside cart's instrumentation, so cart's spans stay fast while every caller's cart hop grows by a fixed amount — which is why cart alerted together with frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator, and checkout a minute later as the slowdown accumulated along the deeper path. Frontend's empty change log rules out a caller-side repoint or rollout as the trigger [tr_fab33a03583f]. The trace evidence appears to contradict this but does not: all ten sampled traces start between 00:56 and 00:59 [tr_ddbe17b074c8], inside a stretch that the attach/remove cycle indicates was unshaped, and none of them reach the 01:03 attach or the 01:07:46 onset. The classification is dependency_latency rather than bad_config because the mechanism is callers blocking on a slow cart, and because the shaping container is an injected delay device rather than a configuration value that names something wrong; remediation is to revert the platform-automation shaping attachment, not to restart or rescale anything.
open_questions: No latency metric was ever retrieved for cart — both metric dispatches returned only the error-ratio template [tr_c28534010e66, tr_f36a7089e42c] — so the ~300ms p50/p95 step is inferred from the change record, never directly observed.
No trace sample covers 01:03:28 onward [tr_ddbe17b074c8]; a trace query bounded to 01:03–01:10 would confirm or refute the 300ms step at the caller->cart hop.

Nothing was dispatched against frontend, frontend-proxy, checkout or load-generator telemetry, so the claim that their symptoms are purely downstream of cart rests on topology reasoning, not their own logs or metrics.
Why cart's error ratio fell to zero rather than staying at its ~1% baseline is unexplained; a drop in completed call volume under added latency is one reading, but request rate was never measured.
Whether the shaping applies to egress only or both directions, and whether it covers all cart replicas or one, is not established — this bounds how much of the user-visible latency it accounts for.
Triage reported 14 unmeasured edges; no evidence excludes an independent contributor on the product-catalog or frontend hops that the sampled traces flagged as degrading.

alternatives.root_cause: The real degrading hop is upstream of cart — the sampled traces attribute slowness to load-generator self-time and to frontend/product-catalog hops, not cart.
alternatives.why_not: The traces that support this all start between 00:56 and 00:59, nearly ten minutes before onset and during an interval the attach/remove cycle suggests was unshaped [tr_ddbe17b074c8, tr_af88a5d99977]; they describe pre-incident baseline, and no dispatch examined product-catalog at all, so this is an unexamined hypothesis rather than a supported one.

alternatives.root_cause: The traffic-shaping attach is routine automation noise and the user-visible failure originates in an unexamined caller such as checkout or frontend-proxy.
alternatives.why_not: Checkout alerted a full minute after cart, frontend and frontend-proxy, which is the ordering expected of a victim deeper in the call path rather than an origin; and frontend's change log is entirely empty [tr_fab33a03583f], leaving no mechanism on the caller side against a concrete, temporally matched change on cart [tr_af88a5d99977].

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so nothing should change: cart's error ratio should stay at ~0, cart's logs should continue to show only info-level ValkeyCartStore operations, and the caller-side alerts on frontend, frontend-proxy, checkout and load-generator should persist until the traffic-shaping container is detached by a mechanism this system does not have. The named fix class (config_revert) would be measured as a drop in caller->cart span duration at p50/p95 back to the single-digit-millisecond range seen in [tr_ddbe17b074c8]; I am asserting that no permitted action can produce that effect, not that the effect is unobservable.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if any of the following turns up: (a) the change log holds a prior *configuration* record for cart that revert_config could restore — the board says the only recorded field transition is eth0 delay unset<->300ms, which belongs to a sidecar namespace attachment and not to cart's own env/config [tr_af88a5d99977]; (b) recreating cart's container via revert_config or restart_service would in practice re-create its network namespace and so drop the attached shaper — if the executor's semantics guarantee that, the right move is restart_service on cart and a caller->cart p95 returning to <10ms within ~5 minutes would confirm it; (c) a trace query bounded to 01:03–01:10 shows the 300ms step at the caller->cart hop, raising confidence from medium and justifying escalation to a human with `docker network disconnect` on the shaping container. Note also that every sampled trace so far contradicts the 300ms claim at cart [tr_ddbe17b074c8] and assigns the degrading hop to load-generator or frontend/product-catalog.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is that the incident continues: callers keep paying ~300ms per cart call and the attach/remove cycle may reattach again, so user-visible checkout latency persists with no automated containment. The risk of the alternative — proposing revert_config or restart_service on cart anyway — is worse and concrete: neither action's preconditions are met ([tr_af88a5d99977] explicitly rules out a deploy and rules out a flag/config change on cart, and the evidence points at a change rather than at process state), so the action would recreate a healthy container, discard its cart cache, reset live gRPC connections from frontend and checkout, and leave the shaper attached — a new outage layered on an unfixed one, with the error ratio that is currently flat at zero [tr_c28534010e66] likely rising for the first time in the incident.
proposal.blast_radius: No services are touched. The unresolved condition continues to be seen by cart's callers named in the brief — frontend, frontend-proxy, checkout and load-generator, all of which alerted at or just after onset — and by flagd and the Valkey cart store only as unchanged downstream traffic. Escalation target: whoever owns platform-automation, since it is the actor on all five attach/remove events and the only party that can detach the shaper.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Five services across the checkout path alerted simultaneously with checkout following a minute later, which is a multi-service pattern I cannot dismiss as a single noisy warning. Cart's shared dependency on flagd and the fan-out through frontend make a downstream dependency the cheapest first guess.
